title: Business expenses with proof
description: Keep receipts, trips and notes next to the expenses, so the details can be reconstructed later and a chosen period handed to the accountant.

blocks.text: A working day leaves different traces of spending: a receipt in a bag, a photo on the phone, a note about a trip. When the time comes to gather the paperwork, you have to remember which job each purchase belonged to. A possible idea for an app is to save those links straight away, while the details are still fresh.
Save the expense together with its context

In one review a freelancer describes preparing receipts as a job in itself: glue them to paper, scan them, then send them on. For him the convenience came from shortening that sequence. The example suggests starting with one specific kind of document and carrying it through to a convenient hand-off.

quote.text: I am a freelancer and have to submit receipts for most of my jobs. I used to tape them to a sheet of paper and scan them, which was time-consuming and frustrating. Then I found this app! It saves so much time.

blocks.title: The receipt and the note in one entry
blocks.text: One option is to photograph the receipt and note alongside it which job the purchase was for. After recognition, the date, the amount and the merchant become a draft entry. The original image stays with it: the person can check the values and correct whatever was read wrong.

One period and one project are enough to begin with. That way you can find out which notes are sufficient for the recipient and which fields only slow the entry down. An automatically recognized amount helps fill the card in, but on its own it confirms neither the purpose of the purchase nor that it is correct.

For trips, a purpose is added to the distance and the time. A real estate agent in another review singles out being able to tell personal trips from work ones and then get a list of them for a period. That explains why an automatically collected route history on its own is not enough.

quote.text: I am realtor and I really love this app- I like has it allow me change from personal to business. At the end of the year, I printed out all of business miles for my taxes!

blocks.title: A separate review before export
blocks.text: Before sending, the entries the person hasn’t looked at yet can be shown: recognized receipts, trips with no purpose, expenses with no note. They confirm the details that are needed or correct them. The source material is available on every line, so there is no hunting for a photo separately from an amount.

A review like that will not find anything that was never recorded at all. If a trip was missed or a receipt lost, the app should allow a note to be added and a marker of the gap to be kept. An absence of warnings on the screen should not be presented as a guarantee that the set collected is complete.
Get the set to the recipient

Before building a full tracker, you can assemble a small set with someone who regularly hands in business expenses: the entries for a chosen period, the receipts and the notes. Then ask their accountant to find a few specific expenses and say what is missing for the work to continue. That will show which links between files are actually needed.

The next test is to make one correction and send an updated version in a way the recipient can tell apart. Such a scenario may cut down on hunting for documents again and on follow-up questions; that assumption can be checked against the questions the accountant asks. The requirements for what the materials contain and how they are presented are worth establishing with him before a report template is built.
